children.text: Finally things sync up.  But it's kind of slow.
You know, I don't know why different browsers, different instance of the same browser... they all take different amounts of time to sync up with the YJS database.
It's all kind of ridiculous, if you ask me.
—KJ
Yjs sync speed depends on the
awareness protocol
and
clock drift
between peers. Each browser opens a separate WebSocket to the yjs-server, and they all compete for the same
root

XmlText. When a new client connects, it does a full state vector exchange — the server diffs its document against what the client has and sends back every missing update. If the document is large or has many fragments, that diff takes time.
The ridiculous part: there's no prioritization. A tiny cursor move by one user triggers awareness updates that broadcast to
every
peer, and the sync protocol doesn't distinguish "important structural change" from "someone breathed on the editor." It all goes through the same queue.

What really adds up is when the server has to GC old updates and rebuild the document state. If Chrome loaded and synced while the server was mid-compaction, it gets queued behind the compaction lock. Meanwhile the already-synced instances keep merrily typing.
The fix would be to either use
Y.Doc
's
gc
option or tune the websocket provider's
maxBackoff
and
syncInterval
. Or we could just accept the chaos as the cost of distributed real-time editing.
